Villa Doris Guest House:
Our story

Villa Doris began in 2007, when we bought a neglected ravine in Nono with a 40-year-old adobe house: two bedrooms, a bathroom and a small kitchen-dining area. Little by little we rebuilt it into a cozy cottage for small groups who want to explore the real Ecuador, and the ravine became a garden of native trees and flowers, now home to hummingbirds, birds and other wildlife. 

Villa Doris sits in the village of Nono at 2,875 meters above sea level, surrounded by the Chocó Andino de Pichincha Biosphere Reserve, one of the world’s most biodiverse regions. Here, the mist drifts over the mountains and the days move at the pace of the forest. 

We love what we do and want to share our country with you. Come to Nono, and take home wonderful memories, the warmth of our people and the gratitude of our family, who put their soul into making this place possible. 

Our Villa welcomes up to 12 guests in six comfortable and lovely rooms.

Villa Doris Experiences::
We offer an array of daily activities to explore Nono and the cloud forest 


A day in the clouds (Day Tour)
The village of Nono was the ninth county founded by the Jesuits in the colonial times, and remained as a solitary, almost forgotten town, just 20km northwest of Quito.
Because of this particularity, we can offer you a day tour to an off-the-beaten path destination, where you will learn about Ecuadorian history and culture, meet local people, photograph colorful hummingbirds, wild flowers and bromeliads. Hike while the clouds cover the mountains and the village, giving it a mysterious and mystic touch! 
We will visit Zuro Loma, one of the most important bird reserves in the cloud forest, to have a close encounter with hummingbirds living in high altitude.
Lunch is included at our country house.

2. Nono & the Eco-route of the Hummingbird (2 days / 1 night) 


Just an hour from Quito, this short getaway trades the city for village life, forest paths and a long table at the end of the day. 

Itinerary at a glance: 

Day 1: Transfer Quito – Nono 

After the transfer from Quito, we stroll through the village to meet its people and learn about its history and traditions. We’ll then visit Zuro Loma Bird Reserve, where we’ll discover the fascinating world of hummingbirds and tanagers. Lunch is included.
In the evening, dinner will be prepared and served at Villa Doris. Overnight stay at Villa Doris.

Day 2: Eco-route of the Hummingbird 

After a traditional country breakfast, we set off towards the Tandayapa Valley, observing how the landscape and ecosystems gradually change along the way. Discover lush vegetation, diverse birdlife, and the remarkable adaptations that allow plants and animals to thrive in this unique environment.
We’ll visit a local nature reserve, home to a wonderful variety of hummingbirds and tanagers, where these birds are carefully protected and cared for. Every visit reveals something new, even to those of us who live here. Lunch at a local restaurant, followed by a transfer back to Quito.

3. Eco-route of the Hummingbird (4 days / 3 nights)

Three nights in Nono for those who want to watch the cloud forest change before their eyes. From forests at 3,400 m down to others at 1,400 m, you will find over 20 species of hummingbirds, native flowers and cascading waterfalls along the way.
Day 1: Quito airport – Nono
We transfer you directly from the airport to Nono. Welcome dinner and overnight at Villa Doris.
Day 2: Day tour at protected natural reserves
A morning hike through either Zuro Loma or Yanacocha Reserves, with a box lunch on the trail. In the afternoon, time to wander through the village at your own pace. Dinner and overnight at Villa Doris.
Day 3: Eco-route of the Hummingbird

Spend a full day exploring the lower cloud forest, beginning with a short hike at Pahuma Reserve. Covering 890 acres, Pahuma is a biodiversity hotspot that provides critical habitat for endangered and endemic wildlife, protects vital water sources for nearby communities, and plays a key role in conservation across Ecuador’s Chocó Andino region.
Next, visit a local bird reserve, where colorful birds put on a spectacular natural display. Continue towards Mindo to explore an orchid garden and take part in a cacao workshop. Lunch on your own in Mindo, giving you free time to explore the village’s local restaurants and culinary offerings. 
Return to Villa Doris for dinner and overnight stay.
Day 4: Back to Quito
 Breakfast and transfer to Quito. End of services.

Note:  This program offers the possibility to add on biking or horseback riding tours.
Sustainability:
We choose destinations where communities, nature and responsible travel go hand in hand, and we try to leave every place a little better than we found it. Here is what that looks like in practice. 


Investing where we operate
Inca Holidays invests in the communities it works with. We partner with community-based projects that offer local stays, we hire local guides, offer cultural tours and food experiences.

Community experiences
We work with a few community-based projects that offer local stays, ecotourism, cultural tours and food experiences. Travelers pay a fair price, and the community earns additional income. 

Growing native forest
At Villa Doris we have planted a garden of native tree species, and we encourage and take part in reforestation projects with Alambi Raíces Nativas and Voyages de Rêve. 

Respect
Our guides share the culture and traditions of each place, encourage buying local crafts and taking all rubbish with us. 

Low energy, low noise 
All lighting at Villa Doris is LED to reduce energy use. We also keep noise to a minimum: no parties and no loud music, to protect the peace of our guests and the wildlife.
Gentler cleaning
 We use biodegradable products made with plant-based oils instead of chlorine bleach and petrochemicals, safer for guests, staff and nature.
Refill, don’t buy
 Filtered water dispensers and complimentary refillable bottles mean no single-use plastic bottles for our guests.
Furniture with a second life
 Much of Villa Doris’s charm comes from antiques, refurbished pieces and furniture made from recycled materials. 
From producers to your plate
At Villa Doris, our menus are built around organic, seasonal ingredients from nearby producers, so every dish tastes of the place. We also plan our meals carefully to keep food waste to a minimum.
Amazon Rainforest:
Ecuador’s Amazon Rainforest is a lush world of towering trees, vibrant flowers, giant ferns, and extraordinary wildlife. Home to an incredible diversity of wildlife, the Ecuadorian Amazon offers opportunities to spot colorful birds, butterflies, fascinating insects, howler monkeys, macaws, and, if you're lucky, even the elusive jaguar.
Whether you want to explore remote jungle trails or relax in a hammock surrounded by the sounds of the rainforest, Inca Holidays invites you to discover an unforgettable natural environment. Our carefully selected eco-friendly lodges combine comfort, adventure, and responsible tourism, offering unique opportunities to explore the Amazon while appreciating its extraordinary biodiversity.
Our Amazon experiences are designed for nature lovers, photographers, birdwatchers, and travelers seeking an authentic connection with one of the world's most extraordinary ecosystems

Birding & Photography (4 days / 3 nights )


With approximately 180 bird species to spot, this experience offers exceptional opportunities to observe and photograph some of the region’s remarkable avian diversity.
Day 1: Journey into the Amazon & Flooded Forest
Travel by motorized canoe along the Napo River, keeping an eye out for herons, egrets, vultures, and other bird species along the way. After a packed lunch, continue by paddle canoe through the primary flooded forest of Challwacocha Creek, a habitat for several sought-after Amazonian birds. Upon arrival at the lodge, enjoy a welcome drink, settle into your cabin, and explore the nearby trails or waterways. End the day with a nighttime canoe excursion in search of nocturnal birds.
Day 2: Canopy Birding & Rainforest Trails
Start the day with a canoe ride across Challwacocha Lake and a short walk to the 36-meter observation tower, offering exceptional views of the rainforest canopy and its birdlife. Look for colorful tanagers, toucans, hummingbirds, honeycreepers, and, with luck, the elusive Harpy Eagle. Later, explore the forest understory in search of antbirds and manakins. In the afternoon, continue birdwatching along the Chorongo Trail, where you may encounter species such as the Screaming Piha, Blue-crowned Manakin, and Thrush-like Antpitta.
Day 3: Yasuní National Park & Parrot Clay Licks
Travel by boat along the Napo River to visit the parrot clay licks in Yasuní National Park, where large groups of parrots and parakeets gather to feed on mineral-rich clay. Alternatively, explore the southern area of the park or nearby river islands, searching for bird species that are less commonly found in the northern Amazon. Return to the lodge in the late afternoon for dinner.
Day 4: Final Birdwatching & Departure
Enjoy an early morning canoe ride through Challwacocha Creek, taking in the rainforest at sunrise and looking for any last bird sightings. Then, travel by motorized canoe along the Napo River to El Coca, arriving in time for your flight to Quito. End of services.

Galápagos Islands:
These world-famous islands are home to Ecuador’s first and largest national park, established in 1959. Located approximately 970 km off the coast of mainland Ecuador, the Galápagos archipelago comprises 13 major islands and more than 200 smaller islands, islets, and rocks.
Shaped by volcanic activity, ocean currents, climate, and the arrival of species from the mainland, the islands have developed an exceptional diversity of flora and fauna found nowhere else on Earth. Giant tortoises, blue-footed boobies, flightless cormorants, waved albatrosses, and marine iguanas thrive in this remarkable natural environment, often described as a living laboratory of evolution.

Yacht Catamaran Anahi 

Experience (5 days / 4 nights)


Day 1: Baltra & Santa Cruz Islands: Bachas Beach
Upon arrival at Baltra Island, our guide will welcome you and escort you to Yacht Anahí. After boarding and settling into your cabin, enjoy lunch on board before visiting Bachas Beach, known for its white coral sand and sea turtle nesting sites. Explore a nearby lagoon, home to flamingos and shorebirds, and spot sea lions, marine iguanas, and seabirds along the coast. Return to the yacht for the welcome reception and dinner.

Day 2: Genovesa Island: Darwin Bay & Prince Philip's Steps
Discover Darwin Bay, renowned for its rich seabird diversity, including red-footed and Nazca boobies, swallow-tailed gulls, Galápagos petrels, seabirds, Darwin finches and mockingbirds. After lunch we will continue to Prince Philip's Steps, one of the island's most impressive bird nesting sites, with opportunities for hiking, snorkeling, kayaking, and take a ride in a panga. 
Day 3: Plaza Islands & Santa Fe Island
Explore the Plaza Islands, known for their striking vegetation, sea lions, swallow-tailed gulls, red-beaked sparrows, frigate birds, pelicans and endemic land iguanas resting beneath cacti. Then we will return to the yacht for lunch and a deserved rest. Continue to Santa Fe Island, where scenic trails lead to beautiful viewpoints and opportunities to spot its endemic land iguanas. Enjoy additional opportunities for snorkeling, kayaking, and panga rides.Then we will return to the yacht for dinner.
Day 4: San Cristóbal Island: Punta Pitt, Kicker Rock & Lobos Island
Visit Punta Pitt, an important seabird nesting site where three species of frigatebirds can be observed. After lunch, continue to Kicker Rock (León Dormido), an impressive volcanic formation surrounded by blue-footed boobies, Nazca boobies, and other seabirds. At Lobos Island, enjoy a scenic walk among sea lions and nesting seabirds, followed by snorkeling in calm waters alongside colorful fish and playful sea lions.
Day 5: San Cristóbal Island: El Junco Lagoon or Cerro Colorado
Explore the highlands of San Cristóbal with a visit to either El Junco Lagoon, a freshwater lake nestled within an extinct volcanic crater, or Cerro Colorado Tortoise Breeding Center, where you can observe giant tortoises at different stages of life. Afterwards, transfer to the airport for your return flight to Quito or Guayaquil.

 Experience (8 days / 7 nights)

Day 1- Santa Cruz Island: Highlands
Upon arrival at Baltra Airport, travel across the Itabaca Channel to the highlands of Santa Cruz Island. Enjoy lunch at a private ranch before exploring the lush forests, where you may encounter giant tortoises in their natural habitat. Visit a fascinating lava tunnel formed by ancient volcanic activity before heading to Puerto Ayora to board Yacht Anahí. Enjoy a welcome reception and dinner on board.
Day 2- Isabela Island: Las Tintoreras, Sierra Negra Volcano & Wetlands
Discover Las Tintoreras, a series of small islets surrounded by turquoise waters, where sea lions, marine iguanas, sea turtles, and rays can be spotted. 
Next, we will walk along a path and explore two different beaches. The first beach is a popular place for sea lions and marine iguanas that nest in the area, while the second  beach is surrounded by mangroves. We will disembark to Puerto Villamil and visit the impressive Sierra Negra Volcano, one of the most active volcanoes in the Galápagos. Later, explore the wetlands of Los Humedales, home to a variety of birdlife, and enjoy free time in Puerto Villamil.  At the end of the day we will board the yacht for dinner and a well-deserved rest. 
Day 3 –Isabela Island: Punta Moreno & Elizabeth Bay
Explore Punta Moreno through a scenic 2.1 km trail across volcanic landscapes, offering spectacular views of Isabela's active volcanoes (Sierra Negra and Cerro Azul) and Fernandina Island. Enjoy snorkeling in its rich marine environment before lunch. Then we will visit Elizabeth Bay. Navigate through red mangroves while observing sea turtles, flightless cormorants, rays, sea lions, fish schools and other marine and terrestrial wildlife. After this visit, we will return to the yacht for dinner and rest. 
Day 4 – Isabela Island: Urbina Bay & Tagus Cove
Visit Urbina Bay located at the east base of the Alcedo volcano, where a scenic coastal trail offers opportunities to spot giant land iguanas, Galápagos tortoises, marine iguanas, penguins, blue-footed boobies and flightless cormorants. We will return to the yacht for lunch, followed by a short sailing towards Tagus Cove, for snorkeling or kayaking, followed by a hike to a viewpoint overlooking Darwin Lake, a unique saline lake surrounded by volcanic rocks and petrified rain.
Day 5 - Fernandina Island: Punta Espinoza & Isabela Island: Punta Vicente Roca
Explore Punta Espinoza on Fernandina Island, famous for its large colonies of marine iguanas, flightless cormorants, and Galápagos penguins, falcons and racer snakes. Enjoy snorkeling among marine life, with the possibility of encountering sea turtles and maybe even seahorses. Continue to Punta Vicente Roca on Isabela Island, where you will find clear turquoise water, an exceptional setting for snorkeling. Followed by a panga ride to observe the remains of the volcano, or we may explore a cave that is partially found underwater.Later, celebrate crossing the Equator with a special cocktail on board.
Day 6 – Santiago Island & Rábida Island
Discover Puerto Egas on Santiago Island, a striking black-sand beach where a coastal walk reveals sea lions, marine iguanas, and fascinating tidal pools. Enjoy snorkeling along its rugged coastline before visiting Rábida Island, famous for its distinctive red-sand beach and volcanic landscapes. When we arrive, we will enjoy a snorkeling  activity, in order to learn about the marine life in this area, which is full of interesting aquatic species. Explore a scenic trail leading to a lagoon inhabited by flamingos, finches, pigeons, yellow warblers and mocking birds.
Day 7 – Sombrero Chino Islet & Bartolomé Island
Explore Sombrero Chino, a small volcanic islet known for its lava formations, sea lion colonies, and marine iguanas. Follow a scenic trail and enjoy opportunities for swimming, snorkeling, and kayaking in its beautiful bay where we will be amongst sharks, stingrays, unique species of fish, and occasionally penguins. Continue to Bartolomé Island, home to the iconic Pinnacle Rock. Discover its spectacular volcanic landscapes on a hike to panoramic viewpoints, followed by time to relax and snorkel at one of its beautiful beaches, where penguins, sea turtles, and colorful fish may be spotted.
Day 8 – North Seymour Island
Conclude your Galápagos adventure with a visit to North Seymour Island, renowned for its seabird colonies and unique wildlife. After exploring the island, transfer to Baltra Airport for your return flight, taking home unforgettable memories of the Galápagos Islands.
Ecuadorian Andes:

From traditional clothing and local crafts to the Kichwa language and vibrant festivities, INCA HOLIDAYS invites you to discover the cultural richness of the Ecuadorian Andes through its volcanoes, historic towns, colonial churches, traditional haciendas, and local cuisine.
